thread.title_full: Trump dismisses slumping poll numbers by saying his policies need 'better PR' - NewsBreak

author: Anthony Orrico
title: Trump dismisses slumping poll numbers by saying his policies need 'better PR' - NewsBreak
text:
By Anthony Orrico ,
1 hours ago President Donald Trump on Wednesday continued to dismiss his rapidly declining poll numbers in recent weeks, claiming that many of his policies simply need to be presented to the American people in a better way.
Trump continued to double down on claims that his poll numbers, particularly on the economy, have not been dropping, saying that polls on the economy "should be" great and said he didn't know why they weren't. When pressed on this by NBC News' Tom Llamas, Trump claimed that he had gotten $18 trillion invested in the country and continued to attack his predecessor, former President Joe Biden.
"I have $18 trillion being invested into the country, Biden had less than $1 trillion for four years and the whole country was going to crater," Trump said. "Do you know if [Democrats] won that election, and we won in landslide, this country was, I think it was finished."

Trump placed the blame for his poor poll numbers on bad PR.
“What happens is I think we do a phenomenal job, but we’re bad at public relations,” Trump said during an exclusive interview with NBC News Wednesday night.
Recent average poll numbers compiled by The New York Times, show that Trump's approval rating since taking office last January has been on a steady decline, with only 41% approving of the job he is doing as president, and 55% disapproving
As for issue specific polling numbers, Trump is underwater on two of his key issues, immigration and the economy. Many pundits and experts consider these to be the president's bread-and-butter issues, as many America's cited them as their key concerns when voting in the 2024 election.
A recent Economist/YouGov poll found that only 41% of Americans approved of his handling of the economy, with 55% disapproving.
In the wake of the killings in Minneapolis of Renee Good and Alex Pretti at the hands of federal immigration agents, Trump has started to lose many American's support on the issue of immigration. Scenes of violent crackdowns on protestors and immigrant communities by federal agents have begun to shake American's support for one of the president's historically successful issues.
Recent polls have found Trump's numbers on his handing of immigration have dropped to their lowest point during his second term, with just 39% approving and 53% disapproving, according to a recent, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll.
While these numbers haven't stopped Trump from claiming his poll numbers to be much better than they are, many Americans's aren't buying what the president is selling, and that could spell major disaster for the GOP ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
